reviewer: independent Codex visual reviewer (codex exec, read-only sandbox, fresh session per round)
scope: The 10-second workstation loop, with the rig animating Dave and the screens and a generated clip animating the dog (Seedance 2.0 via the Nous Portal fal gateway, art/dog-ai).

rounds.summary: No blocking compositing defects (no ghosting, halos, seams, broken anatomy, identity drift, dog fading, misregistration or video rectangle); clearly better than the live clip. Asked for larger head yaw, clearer mouse travel or click, distinct typing positions, stronger dog head lift and ear flick, and playback verification.
All four readability fixes RESOLVED with visual evidence; no new blocking defects; desk, keyboard, rug, monitors and character remain registered.
rounds.note: binds the rigged-dog loop, which Dave later rejected for its dog motion; Dave and the screens are unchanged since, apart from 30 -> 24 fps

rounds.summary: After rejecting the rigged dog ("ears don't move like that"), Dave reviewed the generated-dog candidate in a live-vs-new side-by-side and a painting-vs-animated close-up, and approved it for release ("ok").
rounds.equivalence: The committed video differs from the reviewed candidate only in the blend reference (the exact painting rather than the WebP poster) and the encode (CRF 17 rather than 18). In the dog box the mean absolute difference per frame is 1.57 levels (max 1.91).
